purpose: Desired-state registry of bounded privilege grants (sudoers) that agents may propose and only the human operator may install. An agent never applies a grant; it proposes exact file content, the operator reviews and installs, and this file records what SHOULD be present. Observed state comes from `sudo -l` read-back, never from this file.

proposal_convention.rule: Agent proposes the EXACT sudoers file content in a reviewable block plus a risk note (what breaks if abused, how to revoke). Operator installs by hand. Proposal and installation are two separate, individually explicit acts — never one gesture.
proposal_convention.binding: What the operator installs must equal what the agent proposed, verbatim. Any delta is a new proposal.
proposal_convention.revocation: Delete the grant file on the node, remove the entry here. A grant absent from the node but present here is drift (node behind); a grant present on the node but absent here is unauthorized (report, do not silently adopt).
proposal_convention.read_back: After install, `sudo -l -U <user>` on the node must show exactly the granted verbs. Record the check output reference (not the secret) in the entry.

grants.purpose: Runtime-update activation (contracts/runtime-update.json step 5) for canary deploys without per-deploy operator gesture.
grants.read_back_ref: operator-pasted read-back 2026-10-07: visudo -c parsed OK on all sudoers sources; `sudo -n /usr/bin/systemctl is-active cynic-node.service` returned active without password — amended grant (both systemctl paths) functional

permits: disable + stop + active-state read-back of the two soak units only

grants.purpose: Retire the two stale system-scope soak units on builder-119. They were installed from a duplicate repository path (infra/os/systemd/) that was byte-identical to the file on the host (sha256 cf8bdb0e...), and they execute a Cargo-cache binary that does not know the 'supervise' verb, so the parent fails at every boot. The corrected pair runs in the systemd USER scope (/var/lib/cynic/.config/systemd/user) and is active with NRestarts=0. This grant disables and stops the stale pair; it does NOT delete the unit files, which remain a separate operator act.
grants.risk_note: Abuse ceiling: an actor holding this grant can stop and disable exactly two named soak units, and read their active state. It cannot enable them, cannot start other units, cannot write files, and cannot obtain a shell. The soak is not a production role (its own README says so) and the user-scope pair already provides the function, so the availability ceiling is nil. Revoke by deleting /etc/sudoers.d/cynic-soak-retire.

grants.content: user ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/wg show wg0 peers, /usr/bin/wg show wg0 latest-handshakes, /usr/bin/wg show wg0 endpoints, /usr/bin/wg show wg0 allowed-ips, /usr/bin/wg show wg0 transfer, /usr/bin/wg show wg0 listen-port, /usr/bin/wg show wg0 public-key
permits: read-only, key-free views of interface wg0: peers, latest-handshakes, endpoints, allowed-ips, transfer, listen-port, public-key
forbids: `dump` (its first line prints the interface PRIVATE key)
grants.purpose: cortex cannot observe its own WireGuard mesh: `wg show` needs root and `user` has no general sudo, so `cynic network audit` reports 0 peers and `network runtime` reports wireguard_mesh_absent while wg0 is up (10.20.0.3). Observation must be trustworthy before any dashboard or egress node is built on it.
grants.risk_note: Abuse ceiling: an actor holding this grant learns the mesh topology of wg0 (peer public keys, peer endpoints, allowed-ips, handshake times, byte counters). It cannot read the private or preshared keys, cannot change the interface, and cannot obtain a shell. Public keys are not secrets; endpoints are sensitive but not credentials. Revoke by deleting /etc/sudoers.d/cynic-wg-observe. Code follow-up required: current readers call bare `wg ... dump` without sudo; they must move to these key-free verbs through ONE adapter calling `sudo -n /usr/bin/wg`.
